title: Future of settlement and return
excerpt: A boiler on solar panels, how does that work exactly? Discover it in our latest blog. Read on here quickly.
contentHtml:
Electric heating instead of gas

Solar panels are an excellent option for many people to make them more sustainable. By using solar power, less power is required from the grid. However, it is less easy to reduce indoor gas use in this way. Gas is still used for heating in houses where a heat pump is not an option. An easy way to reduce this gas consumption is to use an electric boiler. This boiler heats tap water used for showering and washing dishes. Although the central heating combination still provides heating in the house, solar panels can still reduce gas consumption indoors by an electric boiler.

Use boiler as storage for energy from solar panels

An electric boiler uses power. If a household already has many other devices that also need power, the electric boiler can become quite an extra burden. It would then be useful to make the boiler work when there is little other consumption. In the afternoon, for example, a lot of power is produced while there are few devices on it. Smart boilers can already be set to heat at specific times, but no changes in the weather are taken into account. In this way, a lot of power is still sent to the grid.

This is what the Solar iBoost is for: to make idle solar energy fully available for the electric boiler. Together, the iBoost and the boiler form a WaterAccu, which can indirectly temporarily store the idle current in hot tap water. The Solar iBoost can constantly measure idle current and forward it to the boiler, using as much power as possible.

How does the Solar iBoost work?

The Solar iBoost actually consists of two devices: the box itself that is connected to the boiler, and a measuring clamp with transmitter that is placed in the meter box. The measuring clamp is mounted on the phase wire on which solar power is supplied by the solar panels, between the main switch and the division into groups. If a central heating combination is present, the Solar iBoost and the boiler are connected to the tap water supply of this boiler. When the solar panels produce power, this power is first used by devices connected to the groups.

Unused current is sent to the grid via the phase wire, and this is measured via the measuring clamp. The measuring clamp then signals to the iBoost via radio signal that power is available for the boiler and also how much. The iBoost then controls the boiler to heat with the measured amount of current. This way you can run your boiler on solar panels.

The Solar iBoost increases the power to the boiler in small steps to see if power is delivered back after each step. If so, the power is increased even further. As soon as no power is returned, the power is reduced again. This is constantly alternated. Once the water in the boiler is fully up to temperature, the iBoost stops all power to the boiler. If water can be heated again, the system is reactivated. When used, the preheated tap water first flows through the central heating combination boiler for extra heating if necessary, and then to your shower, kitchen, etc.

How many solar panels do you need to run a boiler on solar panels?

It is somewhat difficult to estimate the amount of solar panels required for this system. This depends on your own use and the number of solar panels you have. For example, a family of 2 people with 10 solar panels will use less power than a family of 4 people with 10 solar panels. However, the Solar iBoost mainly helps to maximize your own use. A family of 4 people with 10 solar panels of 375 Wp per panel uses about 40% of their generated solar energy annually. With a WaterAccu setup, your own use becomes 88%, more than double.

As a result, extra solar panels may not even be necessary, although this naturally differs per situation. Nevertheless, returning electricity will become less advantageous in the future, as netting will be phased out. With the WaterAccu, a boiler on solar panels is therefore an easy step for more efficient personal use.
